title: Mainland Chinese are still driving Hong Kong’s property market despite 20% tax - South China Morning Post
text:
Why mainland Chinese still drive Hong Kong’s housing market despite Beijing’s 20% tax | South China Morning Post Advertisement China property Business Markets Why mainland Chinese still drive Hong Kong’s housing market despite Beijing’s 20% tax 
 After a sharp drop, Hong Kong residential property transactions rebounded by 18.5% in September, with the total value rising by 29.3%
 3 -MIN READ 3 -MIN Listen Chris Tsang Published: 2:00pm, 19 Oct 2026 Although the Chinese government imposed a 20 per cent tax on rental income and capital gains derived from overseas properties transferred into offshore trusts by mainland residents, agents said these investors remained a key driver of the Hong Kong property market. China’s Ministry of Finance and the State Taxation Administration said in July that rental earnings – profits from the sale of properties and investment gains derived from assets including real estate, stocks or equity interests held by mainland Chinese residents through offshore trusts or overseas holding companies – were now subject to individual income tax at a rate of 20 per cent.
 The new rule provides taxpayers with a 90-day compliance window, allowing them to voluntarily declare and pay any outstanding taxes to mainland tax authorities – up until the October 22 deadline – in exchange for an exemption from penalties.
 Kit Lam, senior associate director at Ricacorp Properties, revealed that the new tax regulations announced by mainland China also hit the Hong Kong property market, but the market quickly absorbed the impact.
